intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: You made it! Welcome to the Astronomy Club. Let me show you around our little observatory.
intro.text_zh: 你来了，欢迎加入天文俱乐部。我是玛雅，今晚我带你熟悉这里。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: First, where we are: a ridge in the San Gabriel foothills, 34°N 118°W, 1100 m up - a suburban site, Bortle 5. Los Angeles glows 32 km to the southwest, which is why we face our telescopes north and east.
intro.text_zh: 这里在圣加布里埃尔山麓，北纬 34°、西经 118°，海拔 1100 米。西南边的洛杉矶会照亮天空，所以我们多朝北和朝东观测。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: This is the observation room. The Mission Board on the wall lists tonight's task — check it whenever you feel lost.
intro.text_zh: 墙上是任务板，今晚该做什么都写在那里。忘了下一步，就回来看看。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: The Parts Cabinet stores every lens, mirror and mount we own. The Assembly Table next to it is where you build telescopes from those parts.
intro.text_zh: 左边是零件柜，透镜、镜面和支架都在里面。拿好零件，再去旁边的组装台安装。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: The Observation Pad in the middle is where we actually look at the sky. The Club Logbook keeps a record of every observation you make.
intro.text_zh: 中间的圆台就是观测台。每次看完记得去左下角写日志，之后还能回来对照。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: That terminal on the right is the Stats Terminal — it computes your telescope's magnification, light gathering and field of view from the parts you installed.
intro.text_zh: 右边是数据终端。它会按你装上的零件，算出倍率、集光力和视场。以后我们再用。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Before touching any telescope, we start with the oldest instrument of all: your own eyes.
intro.text_zh: 先别急着碰望远镜。第一晚，我们只用自己的眼睛。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Tonight's goal: walk to the central Observation Pad and find the Moon with your naked eyes. I'll be right here.
intro.text_zh: 走到中央观测台，用肉眼找到月球，再把它移到视野中间。我就在旁边。

level_1_before.speaker: Maya
level_1_before.text_en: Moon first—no telescope yet. It's bright enough for your own eyes.
level_1_before.text_zh: 先找月球吧~这么亮，今晚用眼睛就够了。

level_1_before.speaker: Maya
level_1_before.text_en: Center it, then take your time. Shape first, dark patches second.
level_1_before.text_zh: 移到中央后别急着点完。先看轮廓，再找那些暗色区域。

level_1_after.speaker: Maya
level_1_after.text_en: There we go—your first naked-eye record! Moonlight entered your eye and formed an image on your retina.
level_1_after.text_zh: 有啦，第一份肉眼记录！月光钻进眼睛，最后在视网膜上成了像。

level_1_after.speaker: Maya
level_1_after.text_en: You caught the round disc and dark maria, but the smaller terrain still blurred together. That's normal.
level_1_after.text_zh: 圆盘和暗色月海看见了，小地形却还糊在一起。很正常，不是你眼神不好。

level_1_after.speaker: Maya
level_1_after.text_en: Those dark maria are ancient lava plains. The little pits are impact craters—some have been sitting there for billions of years.
level_1_after.text_zh: 那些暗色月海，其实是古老的熔岩平原。小坑是撞击留下的环形山，有些已经待了几十亿年。

level_1_after.speaker: Maya
level_1_after.text_en: With almost no air or running water, the Moon barely erases those scars. That's why ancient craters can still look so crisp.
level_1_after.text_zh: 月球几乎没有大气和流水，没什么能磨掉这些伤痕。所以很老的环形山也能留到今天。

level_1_after.speaker: Maya
level_1_after.text_en: Your eyes got us this far. Next time, we let a telescope pull those missing edges back out.
level_1_after.text_zh: 肉眼先走到这里。下一晚，我们让望远镜把丢掉的边缘捞回来~

level_2_before.speaker: Maya
level_2_before.text_en: New target tonight: a star. Bright ones meet your eyes halfway; faint ones really don't.
level_2_before.text_zh: 今晚换颗恒星。亮星还肯配合，暗一点的就很会躲呀。

level_2_before.speaker: Maya
level_2_before.text_en: That tiny point is a huge ball of hot gas, making its own light through fusion in the core. Tiny in our sky, not tiny in reality.
level_2_before.text_zh: 等会儿那个小光点，其实是团巨大的炽热气体，核心靠核聚变自己发光。只是离我们太远啦。

level_2_before.speaker: Maya
level_2_before.text_en: Look north for Polaris. Don't wait for a giant sparkle—it will stay a very small point.
level_2_before.text_zh: 朝北找北极星。它不会突然变成大光球，只是一个很小的星点哦。

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: Your eyes are amazing, but they're small light collectors.
level_2_after.text_zh: 找到了吧。眼睛很好用，只是瞳孔这么大，能收集的光终究有限。

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: Polaris itself is about 430 light-years away and roughly 2,500 times brighter than our Sun - it only looks modest because it's so far.
level_2_after.text_zh: 北极星大约在 430 光年外，实际亮度约是太阳的 2500 倍。离得太远，所以眼前只剩一个不起眼的小点。

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: If we want more detail, we need a bigger light collector.
level_2_after.text_zh: 想把更暗的光也收进来，就得用比瞳孔大得多的物镜。

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: The parts cabinet is open. Tomorrow night, we build.
level_2_after.text_zh: 零件柜已经开了。下一晚，我们来装第一台望远镜。

level_3_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_3_before_assembly.text_en: In L1 the Moon was our baseline: bright and obvious, but its dark plains and crater rims blurred together. Tonight we keep the target and change only the instrument.
level_3_before_assembly.text_zh: 还记得第一晚的月球吗？月海能看见，环形山边缘却糊在一起。今晚目标不变，只换工具。

level_3_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_3_before_assembly.text_en: The front objective forms a larger, better-resolved image; the eyepiece lets your eye inspect it. Build the refractor, then compare it with your first log entry.
level_3_before_assembly.text_zh: 物镜负责收光成像，目镜负责放大。先把折射镜装好，再和第一份月球日志比一比。

level_3_after.speaker: Maya
level_3_after.text_en: Now compare: the maria separate from the bright highlands, and the crater rims finally have readable edges.
level_3_after.text_zh: 快对比一下：月海和明亮高地分开了，环形山边缘也终于站出来了。

level_3_after.speaker: Maya
level_3_after.text_en: Keep both sessions in the Club Logbook. The pair tells us more than either pretty view could alone.
level_3_after.text_zh: 两次都别删，放进观测日志一起看。这样望远镜帮了多少，一眼就明白。

level_4_before_focus.speaker: Maya
level_4_before_focus.text_en: Built doesn't always mean sharp. If the image is blurry, wait—don't blame the telescope yet.
level_4_before_focus.text_zh: 装好了也可能会糊。等等，先别怪望远镜，多半只是焦点还没碰上。

level_4_before_focus.speaker: Maya
level_4_before_focus.text_en: Use Q/E gently. Watch the target's edge tighten; if it gets worse, turn back.
level_4_before_focus.text_zh: 用 Q/E 慢慢调。盯着目标边缘，越紧实就越接近；更糊了就反向。

level_4_after.speaker: Maya
level_4_after.text_en: There it is! The crater edge just snapped into place—that's the focal plane.
level_4_after.text_zh: 就是这里！环形山边缘一下咬住了，这才是焦平面。

level_5_before.speaker: Maya
level_5_before.text_en: New observers love the biggest magnification number. I did too. The sky cured me of that pretty fast.
level_5_before.text_zh: 新人最爱追最高倍率，我以前也一样。然后被天空很快教育了一顿，哼。

level_5_before.speaker: Maya
level_5_before.text_en: Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium, with no solid ground to stand on. Its volume could fit more than 1,300 Earths.
level_5_before.text_zh: 木星主要由氢和氦组成，没有能站上去的地面，体积能塞下 1300 多个地球。

level_5_before.speaker: Maya
level_5_before.text_en: If the view holds, look for the Great Red Spot: a storm bigger than Earth, raging for at least 190 years.
level_5_before.text_zh: 画面稳得住，就找找大红斑。那场风暴比地球还大，至少刮了 190 年。

level_5_after.speaker: Maya
level_5_after.text_en: You found the limit: bigger helped only until Jupiter stopped giving you new detail.
level_5_after.text_zh: 你摸到界线了：木星还有新细节时，放大才算有用。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: Now that your telescope zooms in, finding targets gets much harder - the view is a tiny keyhole.
level_6_before.text_zh: 望远镜放大之后，找目标变得难多了——视野只有针孔那么小。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: That is why observers add a FINDER SCOPE. It shows a much WIDER patch of sky than the main telescope.
level_6_before.text_zh: 所以观测者会加装一支寻星镜。它显示的天区比主望远镜宽得多。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: The finder is only for FINDING and CENTERING a target. It gives no planet detail - it is a pointer, not a magnifier.
level_6_before.text_zh: 寻星镜只用来寻找和把目标移到中心。它看不到行星细节——它是瞄准器，不是放大镜。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: The routine is: aim with the wide finder first, center the target, THEN switch to the main telescope to observe it up close.
level_6_before.text_zh: 先用寻星镜把它抓进来，再切主镜细看。别一上来就用窄视野硬找。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: But a finder is only trustworthy once it POINTS THE SAME WAY as the main scope. Tonight you will calibrate it on Sirius.
level_6_before.text_zh: 但寻星镜只有在与主镜指向一致时才可靠。今晚你要在天狼星上校准它。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: Sirius is a real star 8.6 light-years away - and secretly a two-star system, with a dead white-dwarf companion.
level_6_before.text_zh: 天狼星是一颗 8.6 光年外的真实恒星——而且暗藏玄机，是个双星系统，有一颗死亡后的白矮星伴星。

level_6_after.speaker: Maya
level_6_after.text_en: There—Sirius stayed put in both views. Wide to find, narrow to study.
level_6_after.text_zh: 这次天狼星在两边都没跑。宽视野找路，窄视野看细节~

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: When we pushed the refractor toward very distant, high-contrast targets, you may have noticed colored fringes. A lens bends blue and red light by slightly different amounts, so they do not meet at exactly the same focus.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 当我们用折射镜观测非常遥远、反差强烈的目标时，你可能注意到了彩色边缘。透镜对蓝光和红光的折射程度略有不同，因此它们不能在完全相同的位置聚焦。

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: A Newtonian reflector replaces the objective lens with a curved primary mirror. Reflection sends all visible colors along the same geometric path, removing lens chromatic aberration.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 牛顿反射镜用弯曲主镜代替物镜。反射让各种可见光沿同一条几何光路前进，因此不会产生透镜色差。

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: The primary mirror gathers and focuses the light. A small diagonal secondary redirects it to the side focuser and eyepiece. Study that path, then build it yourself.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 主镜负责集光并聚焦，小型斜副镜再把光转向侧置调焦座和目镜。先看懂这条光路，然后亲手把它组装出来。

level_7_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_7_before_assembly.text_en: Tonight's nebula is faint, and our 60 mm objective is running out of light before you are running out of skill.
level_7_before_assembly.text_zh: 今晚的星云太淡，60mm 物镜先到极限了。不是你不会看，是它收的光不够。

level_7_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_7_before_assembly.text_en: Swap in the 100 mm objective; it gathers nearly three times as much light. Rebuild the refractor, then take it toward Orion.
level_7_before_assembly.text_zh: 换上 100mm 物镜吧，它能收近三倍的光。重新装好折射镜，再去找猎户座。

level_7_after.speaker: Maya
level_7_after.text_en: That brighter patch is the aperture at work. Faint targets need more collected light, not empty magnification.
level_7_after.text_zh: 那团更亮的淡光，就是大口径的功劳。暗目标缺的是光，不是一个更大的模糊影子。

level_8_before.speaker: Maya
level_8_before.text_en: A nebula is a huge cloud of gas and dust—sometimes glowing, sometimes blocking light. Orion is a stellar nursery about 1,344 light-years away.
level_8_before.text_zh: 星云是大片气体和尘埃，有的发光，有的挡光。猎户座大星云离我们约 1344 光年，还是座恒星育婴房。

level_8_before.speaker: Maya
level_8_before.text_en: It won't behave like the Moon. Keep the field wide and feed your eyes light; don't bully it with magnification.
level_8_before.text_zh: 它可不像月亮那么大方。视野留宽一点，多收光，别拿高倍率吓它呀。

level_8_before.speaker: Maya
level_8_before.text_en: New stars are forming inside that faint glow right now. Soft-looking, yes. Empty, absolutely not.
level_8_before.text_zh: 新的恒星正在那团淡光里出生呢。看着轻飘飘，里面可一点都不空。

level_8_after.speaker: Maya
level_8_after.text_en: You gave it enough light, and Orion's faint shape finally came out. Save that view.
level_8_after.text_zh: 光收够以后，猎户座星云的淡轮廓真的冒出来了。快记进日志，我要留着比~

level_9_before.speaker: Maya
level_9_before.text_en: Andromeda sits far beyond the Milky Way. Through this telescope, it may greet you as one very shy smudge.
level_9_before.text_zh: 仙女座远在银河系外。进了目镜，也可能只肯露一团很害羞的淡光。

level_9_before.speaker: Maya
level_9_before.text_en: Don't chase a poster image. Finding that honest faint glow is tonight's real job.
level_9_before.text_zh: 别等海报级大旋涡。能认出那团真实的微光，今晚就做对了。

level_9_before.speaker: Maya
level_9_before.text_en: A galaxy is a whole city of stars held together by gravity. Andromeda may contain roughly a trillion of them.
level_9_before.text_zh: 星系像一整座被引力拢住的恒星城。仙女座这一座，可能就有约一万亿颗恒星。

level_9_before.speaker: Maya
level_9_before.text_en: It's about 2.5 million light-years away and moving toward us. In roughly 4 billion years, Andromeda and the Milky Way are expected to merge.
level_9_before.text_zh: 它离我们约 250 万光年，却还在慢慢靠近。大约 40 亿年后，它和银河系预计会合并。

level_9_after.speaker: Maya
level_9_after.text_en: You pulled Andromeda out of that dark field. All right—now your name really belongs in the Club Logbook.
level_9_after.text_zh: 你把仙女座从暗空里捞出来了。好啦，现在你的名字真的该写进观测日志。

level_9_after.speaker: Maya
level_9_after.text_en: Welcome aboard, little observer. Keep a pen near the log desk—you'll need it.
level_9_after.text_zh: 欢迎入队，小观测员~日志桌旁那支笔，以后可要常用了。

level_10_before.speaker: Maya
level_10_before.text_en: Jupiter again, but with a sneaky question: when does more power stop helping?
level_10_before.text_zh: 又是木星，不过问题有点坏：倍率加到哪里，会开始帮倒忙？

level_10_before.speaker: Maya
level_10_before.text_en: Raise the magnification step by step. Watch brightness, steadiness, and detail—not just size.
level_10_before.text_zh: 一档档往上加吧。别只看大小，也盯住亮度、稳定和细节。

level_10_after.speaker: Maya
level_10_after.text_en: Bigger is not clearer. You proved it yourself tonight.
level_10_after.text_zh: 更大不等于更清楚。今晚你亲手证明了。

level_11_before.speaker: Maya
level_11_before.text_en: Mars again—but tonight it's skimming the horizon, right through the messiest air.
level_11_before.text_zh: 又见火星，不过今晚它贴着地平线，正泡在最乱的那层空气里。

level_11_before.speaker: Maya
level_11_before.text_en: Mars is a rocky world about half Earth's size. That rusty color comes from iron-oxide dust.
level_11_before.text_zh: 火星是颗岩石行星，大小约为地球一半。那身铁锈红，来自氧化铁尘埃。

level_11_before.speaker: Maya
level_11_before.text_en: Tonight, watch the seeing. Turbulent air bends the light around, like the shimmer above a hot road.
level_11_before.text_zh: 今晚盯的是视宁度。空气一乱，光就像隔着热浪一样晃呀晃。

level_11_before.speaker: Maya
level_11_before.text_en: A low Mars sends its light through much more atmosphere. If it looks mushy, don't accuse the optics yet—the air is the troublemaker.
level_11_before.text_zh: 火星这么低，光要穿过更厚的大气。画面发软先别拆镜子，捣乱的是空气。

level_11_before.speaker: Maya
level_11_before.text_en: If the image boils instead of staying steadily blurry, lower the magnification and wait for a calmer moment.
level_11_before.text_zh: 如果画面一阵清楚一阵沸腾，就先降倍率，等空气安分一点。

level_11_after.speaker: Maya
level_11_after.text_en: You caught it: low Mars was swimming in thick air. Lower power gave you the steadier view.
level_11_after.text_zh: 判断对啦：低空火星泡在厚空气里。倍率退一点，画面反而稳住了。

level_11_after.speaker: Maya
level_11_after.text_en: Unsteady air puts a hard ceiling on useful magnification. Push past it and you only enlarge the blur.
level_11_after.text_zh: 空气不稳时，有效倍率就有硬上限。再往上推，放大的只是模糊。

level_11_after.speaker: Maya
level_11_after.text_en: Keep tonight's boiling edge in mind. Next time a low target does this, check the sky before blaming your hands.
level_11_after.text_zh: 记住今晚这种沸腾的边缘。以后低空目标又这样，先看天况，别先怪自己。

level_12_before.speaker: Maya
level_12_before.text_en: Back to the Moon. It's bright enough to make high magnification earn its dinner.
level_12_before.text_zh: 回到月球~它够亮，高倍率这次终于有饭吃了。

level_12_before.speaker: Maya
level_12_before.text_en: Change eyepieces as you climb, but refocus every time. The old focal point won't follow along politely.
level_12_before.text_zh: 换目镜往上加倍率吧，不过每换一次都要重调焦。旧焦点才不会乖乖跟过来。

level_12_before.speaker: Maya
level_12_before.text_en: The seeing is average tonight—still a little shimmer, but nothing like that low Mars session.
level_12_before.text_zh: 今晚视宁度一般，会有一点晃，但没低空火星那晚那么折腾。

level_12_before.speaker: Maya
level_12_before.text_en: The Moon has almost no atmosphere to burn up incoming rocks. Even small impactors can reach the ground and leave a crater.
level_12_before.text_zh: 月球几乎没有大气替它烧掉来袭岩石。小撞击体也能直达地面，留下环形山。

level_12_before.speaker: Maya
level_12_before.text_en: Now raise the power and refocus. Let's see which crater rims the Moon is willing to give back.
level_12_before.text_zh: 现在加倍率，再重新调焦。看看月球肯把哪些环形山边缘交出来。

level_12_after.speaker: Maya
level_12_after.text_en: Those crater rims really did sharpen. Same rule, different target: brightness paid for the power.
level_12_after.text_zh: 环形山边缘真的更清楚了。还是那条规则：亮度替高倍率买了单。

level_12_after.speaker: Maya
level_12_after.text_en: A faint target under the same seeing would have fallen apart. The Moon's brightness is what kept the detail alive.
level_12_after.text_zh: 换成暗目标，同样的视宁度早就糊掉了。是月球的亮度把细节撑住了。

level_12_after.speaker: Maya
level_12_after.text_en: Bright lunar detail likes power; a faint galaxy often wants the opposite. Pocket that trade-off—we'll need it soon.
level_12_after.text_zh: 亮月球喜欢倍率，暗星系往往正相反。这条权衡先揣好，后面马上要用。

level_13_before.speaker: Maya
level_13_before.text_en: Your call tonight: choose the target and the power. I'll be back in the hall waiting for your log.
level_13_before.text_zh: 今晚你说了算：目标和倍率都自己选。我回大厅等你的观测日志~

level_13_before.speaker: Maya
level_13_before.text_en: The seeing is average: no drama, just that small shimmer you already know how to read.
level_13_before.text_zh: 今晚视宁度一般，没新花样，就是你已经认得的那点小晃动。

level_13_before.speaker: Maya
level_13_before.text_en: No hint circle this time. Make a plan, trust your eyes, and change course if the evidence says so.
level_13_before.text_zh: 这次没有提示圈。先定个计划，信自己的眼睛；证据不对，就换策略。

level_13_before.speaker: Maya
level_13_before.text_en: Planet, Moon, or star—start low, hold the target steady, then add only as much power as the view can support.
level_13_before.text_zh: 行星、月球还是恒星都一样：先低倍率稳住，再一点点加到画面能承受的位置。

level_13_after.speaker: Maya
level_13_after.text_en: That choice had a reason behind it. Now you're observing, not just trying buttons.
level_13_after.text_zh: 你这次的选择有理由，不是在碰运气按按钮。嗯，真的开始像观测者了。

level_13_after.speaker: Maya
level_13_after.text_en: Magnification Mastery is yours. Next problem: a perfect view is useless if the target never enters it.
level_13_after.text_zh: 「倍率掌握」徽章归你。下一题：画面再好，找不到目标也白搭呀。

level_13_after.speaker: Maya
level_13_after.text_en: Whatever you chose, the rule held: match the power to the object and the sky, not your ambition.
level_13_after.text_zh: 不管你选了谁，规则都一样：倍率要配目标和天况，不是配野心~

level_14_before.speaker: Maya
level_14_before.text_en: Third visit to Mars. This time, no lucky sweeping—we're giving the sky an address.
level_14_before.text_zh: 第三次找火星。这回不靠乱扫碰运气，我们给天空写个地址。

level_14_before.speaker: Maya
level_14_before.text_en: Azimuth tells you which way around; altitude tells you how high. Follow both and Mars has nowhere to hide.
level_14_before.text_zh: 方位角管朝哪边，俯仰角管抬多高。两个数都跟上，火星就躲不掉。

level_14_before.speaker: Maya
level_14_before.text_en: The air is calm, so navigation gets the whole stage tonight. Very considerate of the sky, honestly.
level_14_before.text_zh: 今晚空气很安分，导航可以独占舞台。难得天空这么给面子~

level_14_before.speaker: Maya
level_14_before.text_en: Mars also has two tiny, lumpy moons: Phobos and Deimos. They may be captured asteroids, though their origin is still debated.
level_14_before.text_zh: 火星还有两颗小小的卫星：火卫一和火卫二。它们可能是被捕获的小行星，不过来源还在争论。

level_14_after.speaker: Maya
level_14_after.text_en: You walked the numbers straight to Mars. Coordinates really do turn the sky into an address book.
level_14_after.text_zh: 你顺着数字直接走到火星了。坐标真的能把天空变成地址簿呀。

level_14_after.speaker: Maya
level_14_after.text_en: No luck and no turbulence to hide behind—just the numbers and your steady corrections. Clean work.
level_14_after.text_zh: 没靠运气，也没拿空气当借口，只有坐标和你那几下稳稳的修正。漂亮。

level_14_after.speaker: Maya
level_14_after.text_en: Once Az/Alt makes sense, even an empty patch of sky has directions. Keep that skill close.
level_14_after.text_zh: 读懂方位角和俯仰角以后，再空的天区也有路标。这招收好，会常用的。

level_15_before.speaker: Maya
level_15_before.text_en: A fresh finder tells tiny lies. Let's teach it to agree with the main scope.
level_15_before.text_zh: 刚装上的寻星镜会撒点小谎。来，教它和主镜说同一句实话。

level_15_before.speaker: Maya
level_15_before.text_en: Center a bright star in the main scope first, then nudge the finder onto that exact same star.
level_15_before.text_zh: 先让亮星在主镜居中，再微调寻星镜，让它也压住同一颗星。

level_15_before.speaker: Maya
level_15_before.text_en: The sky is calm enough that any remaining offset belongs to the finder. One problem at a time—my favorite kind.
level_15_before.text_zh: 今晚天况够稳，剩下的偏差就归寻星镜。一次只处理一个问题，我最喜欢这种夜晚。

level_15_before.speaker: Maya
level_15_before.text_en: Even half a degree of error can send a high-power view into the wrong neighborhood. Small offset, huge annoyance.
level_15_before.text_zh: 哪怕只偏半度，高倍率也会把你送去隔壁天区。小误差，超级烦。

level_15_after.speaker: Maya
level_15_after.text_en: Both crosshairs landed on the same star. Your wide eye and narrow eye finally agree.
level_15_after.text_zh: 两副准星都压住同一颗星啦。宽眼睛和窄眼睛，终于不吵架了。

level_15_after.speaker: Maya
level_15_after.text_en: Do that once at the start of a session and the finder earns your trust for the night.
level_15_after.text_zh: 每晚开工前校准一次，之后寻星镜才值得你信任。

level_15_after.speaker: Maya
level_15_after.text_en: Skip it, and you can spend an hour searching the right pattern around the wrong center. Ask me how I know.
level_15_after.text_zh: 跳过它，你可能围着错误中心找一小时。别问我怎么知道的，哼。

level_16_before.speaker: Maya
level_16_before.text_en: Feeling confident, little observer? Try the main scope alone first.
level_16_before.text_zh: 很有自信嘛，小观测员？先试试只靠主镜找它。

level_16_before.speaker: Maya
level_16_before.text_en: The air is calm, so this one is purely about workflow. If the target slips away, you already know the recovery route.
level_16_before.text_zh: 今晚空气很稳，难点只在流程。目标丢了也别慌，你已经知道回哪一步。

level_16_before.speaker: Maya
level_16_before.text_en: Six degrees feels enormous when you don't know where you're aimed. Give it one honest solo try.
level_16_before.text_zh: 不知道朝哪儿时，6 度视野也能大得吓人。先自己认真试一次吧。

level_16_before.speaker: Maya
level_16_before.text_en: No finder and no hint circle on that first attempt. If you get lost, stop sweeping wildly and come back for the wide-field step.
level_16_before.text_zh: 第一次先不用寻星镜和提示圈。真迷路了就停手，别乱扫，再回到宽视野那一步。

level_16_mid.speaker: Maya
level_16_mid.text_en: Lost? Of course—you tried to navigate through a keyhole. Reset: wide first, narrow last.
level_16_mid.text_zh: 迷路了吧？拿钥匙孔当地图，谁都会丢。重来：先宽后窄。

level_16_after.speaker: Maya
level_16_after.text_en: There it is—Jupiter back in the main view. Narrow shows detail; wide shows the way.
level_16_after.text_zh: 看，木星回到主镜里了！窄视野看细节，宽视野负责认路。

level_16_after.speaker: Maya
level_16_after.text_en: Jupiter has more than 100 officially recognized moons. The big four—Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto—can appear as tiny points beside it.
level_16_after.text_zh: 木星已有 100 多颗获正式确认的卫星。最大的四颗——木卫一、二、三、四——会像小光点排在旁边。

level_16_after.speaker: Maya
level_16_after.text_en: Everybody gets lost this way once. Now you know how to recover without turning the whole telescope inside out.
level_16_after.text_zh: 这种迷路谁都经历过。现在你会自己找回来，不用把整台镜子拆了泄愤啦。

level_17_before.speaker: Maya
level_17_before.text_en: Tonight, the sky is yours. I'll be in the hall pretending not to worry about the clouds.
level_17_before.text_zh: 今晚天空交给你。我在大厅里，假装一点都不担心外面的云。

level_17_before.speaker: Maya
level_17_before.text_en: Thin cloud is drifting through. The target will dim and brighten as each patch passes—that's weather, not a loose cable.
level_17_before.text_zh: 薄云正在飘。目标会跟着云块忽暗忽亮——这是天气，不是哪根线松了。

level_17_before.speaker: Maya
level_17_before.text_en: Waiting for a cloud gap is observing, not failing. Sometimes the smartest adjustment is leaving the controls alone.
level_17_before.text_zh: 等云缝也是观测，不叫失败。有时最聪明的操作，就是先别碰控制器。

level_17_before.speaker: Maya
level_17_before.text_en: The seeing is average and the hint circle is gone. Use the finder, focus, then wait for a clean window.
level_17_before.text_zh: 今晚视宁度一般，提示圈也撤掉了。寻星、调焦，再等一个干净窗口。

level_17_after.speaker: Maya
level_17_after.text_en: You found the target without a trail of hints. That badge is properly earned.
level_17_after.text_zh: 没铺提示路，你还是把目标找到了。这个徽章拿得很踏实。

level_17_after.speaker: Maya
level_17_after.text_en: Better yet, you waited for the cloud gap instead of mistaking dimming for broken gear. That patience matters on faint targets.
level_17_after.text_zh: 更重要的是，你没把云遮造成的变暗怪到设备头上，还等到了云缝。暗目标就需要这份耐心。

level_17_after.speaker: Maya
level_17_after.text_en: Sky Navigator, logged. Next we go after the shy, faint stuff—bring patience.
level_17_after.text_zh: 「星空导航」记进日志。接下来追那些害羞的暗目标，耐心也要带上哦。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: Orion again, but tonight we change what counts as success. Deep-sky work is honest before it is pretty.
level_18_before.text_zh: 还是那片猎户座星云。今晚先别追求漂亮，能诚实认出那团淡光就算成功。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: A nebula won't hand you a crisp outline like the Moon. A steady faint smudge is real evidence.
level_18_before.text_zh: 星云不会像月球那样送你利落边缘。稳稳的一团淡光，本身就是证据。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: Thin haze and average seeing will soften an already faint target. If the glow breathes with the air, don't chase it with the focus knob.
level_18_before.text_zh: 薄雾和一般视宁度会让它更软。淡光跟着空气一阵阵变化时，别拿调焦旋钮追它。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: Fair quality is enough tonight. Record what the sky actually gives you, not the detail you hoped to see.
level_18_before.text_zh: 所以今晚“尚可”就够啦。只记天空真的给你的，别替它脑补细节。

level_18_after.speaker: Maya
level_18_after.text_en: You held onto light that traveled about 1,300 years. Soft, faint, and unmistakably there.
level_18_after.text_zh: 你真的留住了跑来约 1300 年的光。很淡，很软，但它确实在那里。

level_18_after.speaker: Maya
level_18_after.text_en: Recognizing that honest glow without forcing sharp edges is a real observing skill.
level_18_after.text_zh: 没硬把它想成锐利图案，还认出了真实淡光。这就是本事呀。

level_18_after.speaker: Maya
level_18_after.text_en: Bright planets announce detail; nebulae ask for patience, contrast, and realistic expectations—not brute-force power.
level_18_after.text_zh: 亮行星会主动交细节，星云却要耐心和对比度。靠蛮加倍率可请不动它。

level_19_before.speaker: Maya
level_19_before.text_en: Orion again—this time we treat it like a proper experiment.
level_19_before.text_zh: 第三次看猎户座星云。这回认真做个对照实验~

level_19_before.speaker: Maya
level_19_before.text_en: Same nebula, same kind of sky. Change only the aperture, or the comparison tells us nothing.
level_19_before.text_zh: 星云和天况都尽量不变，只换口径。变量一多，结果就说不清啦。

level_19_before.speaker: Maya
level_19_before.text_en: The forecast gave us a cloud-free window with similar seeing. Perfect: a fair test changes one variable at a time.
level_19_before.text_zh: 预报刚好给了无云窗口，视宁度也和上次接近。很配合嘛，一次只改一个变量。

level_19_before.speaker: Maya
level_19_before.text_en: Fit the larger objective, then bring back what changed. We're testing collected light, not wishful thinking.
level_19_before.text_zh: 先换上大口径物镜，再把变化带回来。我们测的是集光，不是愿望呀。

level_19_after.speaker: Maya
level_19_after.text_en: Last time, a smudge; this time, a shape. That extra structure is aperture at work.
level_19_after.text_zh: 上次是一团斑，这次已经有形状了。多出来的结构，就是口径在干活。

level_19_after.speaker: Maya
level_19_after.text_en: Magnification and sky stayed comparable; only the objective changed. That's why this result actually means something.
level_19_after.text_zh: 倍率和天况都可比，只换了物镜。所以这次变亮，才真的能说明问题。

level_19_after.speaker: Maya
level_19_after.text_en: Put this in the log: when a target is light-starved, check aperture before chasing focus or power.
level_19_after.text_zh: 写进日志：目标缺光时，先查口径，别急着追倍率和焦点。

level_20_before.speaker: Maya
level_20_before.text_en: Andromeda again. Tonight the trouble is streetlight glow, not your telescope and definitely not your hands.
level_20_before.text_zh: 又见仙女座。今晚捣乱的是城市灯光，不是望远镜，更不是你的手。

level_20_before.speaker: Maya
level_20_before.text_en: Andromeda is huge, but the bright city background swallows its faint outer glow.
level_20_before.text_zh: 仙女座其实很大，可明亮的城市背景会吞掉它暗淡的外缘。

level_20_before.speaker: Maya
level_20_before.text_en: It's like looking for fireflies in a fully lit room. They're still there; the bright background steals the contrast.
level_20_before.text_zh: 就像在灯全开的房间里找萤火虫。它们没消失，只是背景太亮，微光没了对比。

level_20_before.speaker: Maya
level_20_before.text_en: Andromeda spans about six full-Moon widths in our sky, but most of it is too faint here. City glow leaves only the bright core.
level_20_before.text_zh: 仙女座在天空中约有六个满月那么宽，可大部分太暗。城市光一压，只剩明亮核心。

level_20_before.speaker: Maya
level_20_before.text_en: So stop chasing the focuser. If the core is sharp but the galaxy is missing, the sky is the limit.
level_20_before.text_zh: 所以先别追着调焦。核心清楚、外缘却不见时，限制来自天空背景。

level_20_after.speaker: Maya
level_20_after.text_en: Nothing was broken. You diagnosed a bright background and recorded the small visible core honestly.
level_20_after.text_zh: 设备没坏。你认出了明亮背景，也老实记下了那个小核心，这就对了。

level_20_after.speaker: Maya
level_20_after.text_en: More aperture can win back some light, but it can't make the city background dark.
level_20_after.text_zh: 大口径能抢回一点光，却没法把城市背景变黑。

level_20_after.speaker: Maya
level_20_after.text_en: For every faint target from now on: check the sky before you put the gear on trial.
level_20_after.text_zh: 以后碰到暗目标，先检查天空，再把设备拉来审问，记住啦。

level_21_before.speaker: Maya
level_21_before.text_en: We hauled the same gear beyond the hills. Darker sky, same Andromeda—let's compare.
level_21_before.text_zh: 我们把同一套设备搬到山那边啦。天更暗，仙女座没变——再比一次。

level_21_before.speaker: Maya
level_21_before.text_en: Remember those fireflies in a lit room? Out here the background is dark enough for the same faint galaxy to separate from it.
level_21_before.text_zh: 还记得亮房间里的萤火虫吗？这里背景够黑，同一个暗星系终于能和天空分开了。

level_21_before.speaker: Maya
level_21_before.text_en: Give your eyes a few quiet minutes. Dark adaptation makes them more sensitive; one bright screen can send that progress backward.
level_21_before.text_zh: 也给眼睛几分钟暗适应。它会越来越敏感，但一眼亮屏就可能倒退哦。

level_21_before.speaker: Maya
level_21_before.text_en: Same telescope, eyepiece, and target. Only the background light changes—so the comparison stays honest.
level_21_before.text_zh: 望远镜、目镜和目标都一样，只改背景光。这样对照才干净。

level_21_after.speaker: Maya
level_21_after.text_en: There are Andromeda's outer hints! The telescope didn't improve overnight; the sky did.
level_21_after.text_zh: 看见仙女座外缘的淡结构了吗？望远镜没一夜升级，升级的是天空。

level_21_after.speaker: Maya
level_21_after.text_en: Same aperture and eyepiece; the upgrade was leaving city glow behind. Dark sky is wonderfully unfair to expensive gear.
level_21_after.text_zh: 口径和目镜都没变，只是离开城市辉光。暗空这项升级，便宜得有点犯规呀。

level_21_after.speaker: Maya
level_21_after.text_en: Deep Sky Observer, logged. Next question: why won't the sky sit still for us?
level_21_after.text_zh: 「深空观测者」记进日志。下一题：天空为什么就是不肯坐好？

level_22_before.speaker: Maya
level_22_before.text_en: That star looks like it's escaping. It isn't—the Earth is turning underneath us.
level_22_before.text_zh: 那颗星像在逃跑？其实不是，是地球在我们脚下转。

level_22_before.speaker: Maya
level_22_before.text_en: Every centered star has always drifted. Low power hides it; high power makes the same motion impossible to ignore.
level_22_before.text_zh: 每颗居中的星其实一直在漂。低倍率把它藏住了，高倍率会让这点移动特别显眼。

level_22_before.speaker: Maya
level_22_before.text_en: Earth turns once in about 24 hours, so the sky appears to move roughly 15 degrees per hour. Tonight, your tracking corrections cancel that apparent drift.
level_22_before.text_zh: 地球约 24 小时自转一圈，天空看起来每小时移动约 15 度。今晚用追踪修正抵消这段漂移。

level_22_before.speaker: Maya
level_22_before.text_en: The seeing is average, so focus on Sirius: correct gently and keep it inside the holding zone.
level_22_before.text_zh: 今晚视宁度一般。轻轻修正，把天狼星留在保持范围里就好。

level_22_after.speaker: Maya
level_22_after.text_en: You kept Sirius centered against Earth's apparent sky motion. Your hands noticed, didn't they?
level_22_after.text_zh: 你把天狼星稳在地球自转造成的视运动里了。手是不是已经有意见啦？

level_22_after.speaker: Maya
level_22_after.text_en: That's why long exposures use tracking motors. Human hands tire and pulse; a good drive keeps making tiny corrections.
level_22_after.text_zh: 所以长曝光要用追踪电机。人手会累、会抖，好的驱动却会一直做小修正。

level_22_after.speaker: Maya
level_22_after.text_en: Next time a target drifts, don't call it random. Read the direction, tune the rate, and let the mount share the work.
level_22_after.text_zh: 以后目标再漂，别当随机故障。看方向、调速率，让支架替你分担。

level_23_before.speaker: Maya
level_23_before.text_en: Tonight the tracking mount holds Vega steady, so your eyes can investigate its edge instead of chasing it.
level_23_before.text_zh: 今晚让追踪支架稳住织女星，你的眼睛就能专心检查它的边缘。

level_23_before.speaker: Maya
level_23_before.text_en: Focus as carefully as you can, then inspect the edge. If the center is sharp but color remains, don't blame your hands.
level_23_before.text_zh: 先调到最佳焦点，再看边缘。中心清楚、彩边还在，就别怪自己的手。

level_23_after.speaker: Maya
level_23_after.text_en: Red on one side, blue on the other—and best focus didn't remove it. That's lens chromatic aberration.
level_23_after.text_zh: 一边红、一边蓝，最佳焦点也赶不走。确认了，这是透镜的色差。

level_23_after.speaker: Maya
level_23_after.text_en: Keep that Vega record. Later we'll compare it with a different optical path and see what changes.
level_23_after.text_zh: 这份织女星记录别删。以后换条光路，我们拿它回来做对照。

level_24_before.speaker: Maya
level_24_before.text_en: One last refractor challenge. Andromeda rewards patience, not frantic corrections.
level_24_before.text_zh: 折射镜最后一关啦。仙女座奖励耐心，可不奖励乱拧控制器。

level_24_before.speaker: Maya
level_24_before.text_en: Aperture, dark sky, focus, tracking—tonight they finally work as one observing plan.
level_24_before.text_zh: 口径、暗空、调焦、追踪，今晚终于要合成一套完整观测计划。

level_24_before.speaker: Maya
level_24_before.text_en: The seeing is average and there is no new trick. Use what you already know and bring back an honest result.
level_24_before.text_zh: 今晚视宁度一般，没有新招。把已经会的用好，再带一份真实结果回来。

level_24_before.speaker: Maya
level_24_before.text_en: Andromeda will drift with Earth's apparent sky motion. Keep it centered; if it slips out too long, settle it again instead of overcorrecting.
level_24_before.text_zh: 仙女座也会随天空视运动漂移。偏出去太久就稳稳拉回，别一着急又修过头。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: From naked eyes to a tracked deep-sky watch - you finished the whole path. Senior Observer.
level_24_after.text_zh: 从肉眼到追踪深空——整条路你走完了。高级观测员。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: You started by looking at the Moon with just your eyes. Look at you now.
level_24_after.text_zh: 你当初只是用肉眼看了看月亮。看看你现在。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: Every telescope you built, every focus you turned, every faint smudge you found - it all led here.
level_24_after.text_zh: 你组装的每一台望远镜，转过的每一次调焦，找到的每一团淡斑——都通向了这里。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: And that galaxy you just held steady? In about 4 billion years it will merge with our own Milky Way. You're watching two galaxies on a slow collision course, one careful look at a time.
level_24_after.text_zh: 而你刚才稳稳看住的那个星系？大约 40 亿年后，它会和我们的银河系合并。你正在一次次耐心的观测中，见证两个星系的缓慢碰撞。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: The club is proud of you, Senior Observer - and the sky doesn't end here. Keep looking up.
level_24_after.text_zh: 俱乐部为你骄傲，高级观测员——但天空的故事不会到此为止。继续抬头看吧。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: One more thing, Senior Observer. We have met a problem the refractor cannot easily solve - and there may be another optical answer in the club storeroom.
level_24_after.text_zh: 还有件事。折射镜的彩边怎么调都在，储藏室里倒是有一种不用大透镜的办法。

1.en: Start with your eyes. Every astronomer begins by learning how to see.
1.zh: 先用眼睛。每个天文学家都是从学会观看开始的。

2.en: Bright stars first. Learn what your eyes can and cannot do.
2.zh: 先找亮星。了解眼睛能做什么、不能做什么。

3.en: Time to build. The objective collects, the eyepiece magnifies.
3.zh: 该动手组装了。物镜收集光，目镜放大图像。

4.en: Blurry is not broken. Turn the knob until it's sharp.
4.zh: 模糊不等于坏了。转动旋钮直到清晰。

5.en: More power is not always more detail.
5.zh: 更高倍率不等于更多细节。

6.zh: 宽视野找目标，窄视野看细节。

7.en: Mirrors gather light too - often more of it.
7.zh: 镜子也能收集光，而且往往收集得更多。

8.en: Faint targets need light buckets, not zoom.
8.zh: 暗目标需要接光桶，而不是放大镜。

9.en: One last target. Make the logbook proud.
9.zh: 最后一个目标。让观测日志为你骄傲。

10.en: Same Jupiter, new question: how much power is too much?
10.zh: 还是木星。这次多换几枚目镜，看看倍率加到哪一档开始得不偿失。

11.en: Mars again - but tonight it hugs the horizon. Low power, steadier view: thick low-altitude air punishes high magnification hardest.
11.zh: 又是火星——但今晚它贴着地平线。倍率低一点，画面稳一点：低空厚重的大气对高倍率的惩罚最狠。

12.en: Back to the Moon - bright enough to take high power, if you refocus first. Average seeing tonight, barely noticeable.
12.zh: 回到月亮——够亮能扛高倍率，但要先重新调焦。今晚只是一般视宁度，几乎感觉不到。

13.en: Your call tonight. Pick a target, pick the power. No hints, just average air.
13.zh: 今晚你说了算。选目标，选倍率。没有提示，只有一般水平的空气。

14.en: Mars a third time - but tonight you navigate by numbers, not by luck. Calm air, pure navigation practice.
14.zh: 第三次找火星——但今晚靠数字导航，不靠运气。空气平静，纯粹练导航。

15.en: Teach the finder scope to point true before you trust it. Calm skies tonight - focus on the calibration.
15.zh: 先教会寻星镜指准，再信任它。今晚天空平静——把注意力放在校准上。

16.en: Tempted to skip the finder? Six degrees is a big place to get lost in.
16.zh: 想跳过寻星镜？6 度视野足够让人迷路。

17.en: No hints tonight. Navigate the whole workflow alone - and learn to wait out a passing cloud.
17.zh: 今晚不画提示圈。自己读坐标、切视野，遇到云就等它过去。

18.en: Same nebula as L7 - but tonight a faint smudge already counts as success. Thin cloud and average seeing both take a bite.
18.zh: 还是那片星云——但今晚看到淡淡的一团就算成功。薄云和一般视宁度都会咬一口亮度。

19.en: Third visit to Orion - this time as a controlled experiment in aperture. Skies are clear tonight on purpose.
19.zh: 第三次看猎户座星云——这次是一场关于口径的对照实验。今晚特意留了晴朗的天空。

20.en: Andromeda again - but the enemy tonight is streetlights, not distance. Light pollution is fireflies in a lit room.
20.zh: 又是仙女座——但今晚的敌人是路灯，不是距离。光污染就像在开灯的房间里找萤火虫。

21.en: Same gear, darker sky. See what a dark sky alone can do - and give your eyes time to adapt.
21.zh: 设备不变，天空更暗。看看纯靠暗天空能带来什么变化——也让眼睛留点时间适应黑暗。

22.en: The Earth keeps turning under you. Keep the star centered as it drifts.
22.zh: 地球一直在你脚下转动。星星漂移时持续把它保持居中。

23.en: Jupiter, fourth time - but tonight the tracking mount does the work. Dial the rate close to 1x.
23.zh: 第四次看木星——但今晚由追踪支架代劳。把速率调到接近 1 倍。

24.en: The final watch. Hold Andromeda steady and finish the whole path.
24.zh: 最后一次练习。稳住仙女座，把前面学过的操作都用上。

25.en: Repeat the Vega observation deliberately: focus, refocus, swap nothing - and confirm the fringe never leaves.
25.zh: 有意重复织女星观测：调焦、再调焦、什么都不换——确认彩边永远不会消失。这是物理，不是失误。

26.en: Build the Newtonian: external supports on the main blueprint, mirrors inside the Optical Tube Assembly, then c
26.zh: 组装牛顿镜：主蓝图装外部支撑，镜筒组件里装镜面，完成准直后对准月球。

27.en: Same star as L23 and L25 - now through mirrors. Compare what the edge of Vega looks like tonight.
27.zh: 和 L23、L25 同一颗星——这次经过的是镜面。比较今晚织女星的边缘。

28.en: Use the side focuser on Saturn. A correct focus separates the pale disk from its ring without false color.
28.zh: 用侧置调焦座对准土星。正确合焦后，淡黄色圆面与光环清楚分开，而且没有虚假彩边。

29.en: Use Albireo as a collimation and angular-resolution test. A well-aligned Newtonian separates its gold and blue components.
29.zh: 用辇道增七检验准直与角分辨率。准直到位的牛顿镜能分开金色与蓝色两颗成员星。

30.en: Push the 150mm mirror to the Crab Nebula. Dark-adapt, use averted vision, and find the torn supernova glow.
30.zh: 把 150mm 主镜推向蟹状星云。完成暗适应并使用侧视法，寻找撕裂状的超新星遗迹微光。

31.en: Use the Newtonian on the Sombrero Galaxy. Hold averted vision long enough to separate its bright nucleus from the dust lane.
31.zh: 用牛顿镜观测草帽星系。保持侧视足够久，把亮核与横穿星系的尘埃带分开。

32.en: Keep Uranus centered through Earth-rotation drift and resolve its tiny blue-green disk.
32.zh: 在地球自转漂移中保持天王星居中并精细调焦，直到蓝绿色光点变成微小而稳定的圆面，而不是背景恒星。

33.en: Poor seeing cannot erase a broad nebula, but sky glow can. Use the nebula filter and wait for the Dumbbell shape.
33.zh: 糟糕视宁度不会抹掉宽广星云，但明亮天空会。使用星云滤镜，等待哑铃状双瓣浮现。

34.en: Betelgeuse through mirrors: a deep orange-red giant with NO false fringe. A refractor would paint its edge blu
34.zh: 用镜面看参宿四：一颗深橙红色的巨星，没有任何虚假彩边。折射镜会给它的边缘涂上红蓝——你的牛顿镜展示的是恒星自己的颜色。

35.en: Complete a precise, filtered observation of the tiny Ring Nebula and prove the 150mm reflector can reveal structure beyond the Solar System.
35.zh: 完成一次精确的环状星云滤镜观测，证明 150mm 反射镜能够显出太阳系之外的结构。

36.en: Build the 200mm Dobsonian and frame the Pleiades with the 30mm eyepiece. The upgrade begins with more light and a deliberately wide field.
36.zh: 装好 200mm 多布森，再用 30mm 目镜框住整个昴星团。大口径收光，宽视场负责把星团完整留下。

37.en: Saturn now appears brighter in the 200mm mirror, but the rocker box has no motor. Nudge, settle, and inspect the rings.
37.zh: 在 200mm 主镜中土星更明亮，但摇箱没有马达。轻推、等待稳定，再检查光环。

38.en: Use the wide-field Dobsonian view to hold both halves of the Double Cluster while manually correcting drift.
38.zh: 利用多布森的宽视场同时容纳双星团两部分，并在漂移中手动修正。

39.en: The 200mm mirror begins to resolve the grainy halo of a cluster 22,200 light-years away.
39.zh: 200mm 主镜开始把 22,200 光年外球状星团的颗粒状外晕分解成恒星。

40.en: Combine 200mm aperture, the 30mm wide-field eyepiece, and a nebula filter to preserve the Lagoon Nebula and its dark lane.
40.zh: 用 200mm 口径配 30mm 目镜和星云滤镜。别把倍率推太高，要把礁湖星云和中间暗带一起留在画面里。

41.en: The same Ring Nebula seen with the Newtonian is brighter now, but passing cloud makes timing the real challenge.
41.zh: 环状星云比上次更亮了，不过云层一直在经过。先稳住目标，等云隙出现再观测。

42.en: Reach the Needle Galaxy about 40 million light-years away and preserve its edge-on dust lane.
42.zh: 用 200mm 主镜观测 NGC 4565。在低空手动保持中同时保住细长侧向星系盘、中央核球与暗尘带。

43.en: Use finder discipline, precise focus, and the 200mm light bucket to distinguish Neptune from the surrounding stars.
43.zh: 运用寻星镜定位、精细调焦和 200mm 集光能力，把海王星从周围恒星中分辨出来。

44.en: Make the hardest Dobsonian hold on M51: dark-adapt, use averted vision, and keep the core and companion together.
44.zh: 在 M51 上完成最难的多布森保持：暗适应、侧视，并让主星系亮核与伴星系共同留在视场中。

45.en: Return to the Dumbbell Nebula and use the 200mm mirror to reveal the faint shell beyond the bright hourglass.
45.zh: 重访哑铃星云，用 200mm 主镜显出明亮沙漏之外的暗弱外壳。

46.en: Build the Cassegrain: a long telescope hidden in a short tube. First light on the Moon through the rear focuse
46.zh: 组装卡塞格林：藏在短镜筒里的长望远镜。通过后置调焦座，用月球开光。

47.en: Long focal length means high magnification. Jupiter looks bigger than ever - if you can find it in the narrow
47.zh: 长焦距意味着高倍率。木星比以往任何时候都大——前提是你能在窄视场里找到它。

48.en: A narrow field punishes sloppy aiming. Use the finder scope discipline you learned long ago.
48.zh: 窄视场惩罚粗糙的瞄准。用上你很久以前学会的寻星镜纪律。

49.en: Mars is tiny. The folded path gives you the scale - the atmosphere decides if you keep it.
49.zh: 火星很小。折叠光路给了你放大倍数——大气决定你能不能保住它。

50.en: High power amplifies every ripple of air. Wait for the still moments; drop power if they never come.
50.zh: 高倍率会放大每一丝大气抖动。等待平静的瞬间；等不到就降低倍率。

51.en: At high magnification the sky drifts FAST across the narrow field. Keep Mars centered.
51.zh: 高倍率下，天空在窄视场里漂移得飞快。让火星保持居中。

52.en: Turn the folded focal length on the Moon: single craters fill the eyepiece.
52.zh: 把折叠焦距对准月球：单个环形山就能填满目镜。

53.en: Same Jupiter, two mirrors: the Newtonian showed a wide bright disk, the Cassegrain a large detailed one. Neith
53.zh: 同一颗木星，两种镜子：牛顿镜给出宽而亮的圆面，卡塞格林给出大而细的圆面。没有谁全面更好。

54.en: Clouds cross a narrow field quickly and completely. Time your observation between them.
54.zh: 云穿过窄视场又快又彻底。在云缝之间安排你的观测。

55.en: Master the folded path under real conditions. Then Maya brings out an even stranger fold - centuries older.
55.zh: 在真实条件下驾驭折叠光路。然后 Maya 拿出一种更奇特的折叠——它还要古老几个世纪。

56.en: Build the Gregorian: light passes through a real focus BEFORE the concave secondary. Alignment must be stricte
56.zh: 组装格里高利镜：光线先穿过一个真实焦点，再到达凹面副镜。对准要求比以往任何一台都严格。

57.en: You observed Sirius with the refractor long ago. Feel where the Gregorian snaps into focus and compare.
57.zh: 很久以前你用折射镜看过天狼星。感受格里高利镜"咔哒"合焦的位置，并做比较。

58.en: The extra focus makes the image upright and high-contrast. Vega, once more, without any fringe.
58.zh: 多出的焦点让成像正立且高对比。再看一次织女星——依然没有任何彩边。

59.en: Small target, strict optics. Every arcsecond of alignment error shows on Mars.
59.zh: 小目标，严苛光学。每一角秒的对准误差都会显现在火星上。

60.en: Study Jupiter's cloud bands: the Gregorian's clean contrast is its quiet strength.
60.zh: 研究木星云带：干净的对比度是格里高利镜低调的强项。

61.en: Can the two-mirror fold handle a faint nebula? Find out on Orion.
61.zh: 双镜折叠能应付暗弱星云吗？在猎户座上找到答案。

62.en: Drift correction through a folded path: keep Sirius centered.
62.zh: 在折叠光路中做漂移修正：让天狼星保持居中。

63.en: Poor seeing on a strict instrument: learn which errors are yours and which are the sky's.
63.zh: 严苛仪器遇上糟糕视宁度：分清哪些误差是你的，哪些是天空的。

64.en: Newtonian, Cassegrain, Gregorian - each fold has a reason. Prove you can explain all three on golden Arcturus.
64.zh: 牛顿、卡塞格林、格里高利——每种折叠都有理由。用金色的大角星证明你能说清这三者。

65.en: The last ground telescope exam. Every mirror you own still fights one enemy: the atmosphere itself.
65.zh: 最后一场地面望远镜考试。你拥有的每一面镜子仍在对抗同一个敌人：大气本身。

66.en: Assemble the segmented space telescope: 18 mirror segments, an infrared instrument package, and a tennis-court
66.zh: 组装分段式空间望远镜：18 块镜片、红外仪器包，和一面网球场大小的遮阳板。

67.en: Infrared is not visible light. Point at Orion and ask a different question: not "what shines" but "what is war
67.zh: 把猎户座对准红外仪器。可见光看发亮的气体，红外会把温暖的尘埃和藏在里面的恒星翻出来。

68.en: Dust blocks visible light but not infrared. Find the newborn stars hiding inside the nebula.
68.zh: 尘埃挡住可见光，却挡不住红外。找到藏在星云内部的新生恒星。

69.en: A warm infrared telescope observes only itself. Manage the sunshield so the instruments stay cold.
69.zh: 发热的红外望远镜只能观测它自己。用好遮阳板，让仪器保持低温。

70.en: Point the telescope AND keep Sun, Earth and Moon behind the shield - both at once.
70.zh: 既要指向目标，又要让太阳、地球和月亮全躲在遮阳板后——两者必须同时成立。

71.en: Andromeda in infrared shows warm dust lanes invisible from the ground. Map them.
71.zh: 红外下的仙女座露出地面看不见的温暖尘埃带。把它们描绘出来。

72.en: Compare tonight's Orion with your Newtonian records: what did the atmosphere steal from you?
72.zh: 把今晚的猎户座和你的牛顿镜记录对比：大气到底偷走了什么？

73.en: Betelgeuse is cool and red - a natural infrared beacon. Measure the giant.
73.zh: 参宿四又冷又红——天生的红外灯塔。测量这颗巨星。

74.en: Deploy, cool, point, observe: run a complete infrared session by yourself.
74.zh: 这次你自己来：展开、降温、指向，再开始曝光。我只在旁边看着。

75.en: You now observe light no eye can see. There is radiation even "colder" than infrared - and for that, we have a
75.zh: 你已能观测眼睛看不见的光。还有比红外"更冷"的辐射——为了它，我们在贵州有一个巨人。

76.en: Set up FAST: active dish, suspended feed cabin, signal processor. There is no eyepiece - there never will be.
76.zh: 搭建 FAST：主动反射面、悬吊馈源舱、信号处理器。这里没有目镜——永远不会有。

77.en: Sweep the frequency band until the pulsar's repeating pulse rises out of the noise.
77.zh: 扫过频段，直到脉冲星重复的脉冲从噪声中浮现。

78.en: Read the trace and measure the period: 0.714 seconds per revolution of a dead star.
78.zh: 读取轨迹并测量周期：一颗死亡恒星每 0.714 秒自转一圈。

79.en: A radio telescope points with signal strength. Move the feed until the pulse peaks - that is your pulsar.
79.zh: 射电望远镜靠信号强度指向。移动馈源直到脉冲最强——那就是你的脉冲星。

80.en: Tonight the pulse barely clears the noise floor. Tune finer, read more carefully.
80.zh: 今晚脉冲勉强高出噪声底。调得更细，读得更仔细。

81.en: Longer listening makes faint pulses add up. Radio astronomy rewards patience with certainty.
81.zh: 听得更久，微弱脉冲就会累加起来。射电天文用确定性回报耐心。

82.en: The feed cabin hangs from cables above the dish. Practice fine positioning against a moving sky.
82.zh: 馈源舱靠缆索悬在反射面上方。练习在移动的天空下做精细定位。

83.en: Interference is radio astronomy's light pollution. Learn to tell the pulsar from human noise.
83.zh: 干扰就是射电天文的光污染。学会把脉冲星和人造噪声区分开。

84.en: Tune, localize, measure, record - one complete radio observation, alone.
84.zh: 先调到合适频段，再定位、测量和记录。今晚这套射电观测由你独立完成。

85.en: Data IS the observation - you have proven it. One question remains: what happens when every window opens at on
85.zh: FAST 不会给你一张漂亮照片。它给你的是曲线、脉冲和重复出现的信号。接下来，把它和可见光、红外放在一起看。

86.en: One nebula, three observatories. Decide which instrument answers tonight's question.
86.zh: 还是同一片星云，但三台仪器看见的东西不同。先看今晚要找什么，再选观测台。

87.en: Observe Orion in visible light and infrared, and note what each reveals that the other hides.
87.zh: 分别用可见光和红外观测猎户座，记下彼此揭示与隐藏的东西。

88.en: Stars in visible light, dust in infrared, cold gas in radio: three portraits of one galaxy.
88.zh: 可见光里的恒星、红外里的尘埃、射电里的冷气体：同一个星系的三幅肖像。

89.en: Lay the three records side by side. What claim does EVERY window support?
89.zh: 把三份记录并排看看。哪些结构每个波段都看见了，哪些只在某一边出现？

90.en: No instructions this time. Pick the question, pick the instrument, run the observation.
90.zh: 这次我不发操作口令了。先想清楚要看什么，再选仪器、完成观测。

91.en: Everything you have learned, in one report: one galaxy, every window of light, one supported conclusion.
91.zh: 最后写一份报告。把同一个星系在可见光、红外和无线电里的样子说清楚。

level_25_before.speaker: Maya
level_25_before.text_en: Tonight's target is Vega — a brilliant blue-white star. Your refractor skills are solid now, so I want you to do something new: look CLOSELY at the star's edge.
level_25_before.text_zh: 今晚的目标是织女星——一颗明亮的蓝白色恒星。你的折射镜已经用得很熟练了，所以这次我要你做一件新的事：仔细看恒星的边缘。

level_25_before.speaker: Maya
level_25_before.text_en: Focus as carefully as you can. If you see anything strange around the star, don't assume you made a mistake. Just observe it, and remember it.
level_25_before.text_zh: 尽你所能仔细调焦。如果你在恒星周围看到什么奇怪的东西，不要以为是自己操作错了。观察它，记住它。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: You saw it: a red fringe on one side, blue on the other. That is chromatic aberration — and it is NOT your fault.
level_25_after.text_zh: 你看到了：一侧偏红、一侧偏蓝的彩色边缘。这叫色差——而且这不是你的错。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: A glass lens bends blue light more strongly than red light, so they can never land on exactly the same focal point. No eyepiece swap or focusing can fully fix it.
level_25_after.text_zh: 玻璃透镜对蓝光的偏折比红光更强，所以它们永远无法落在完全相同的焦点上。换目镜、再调焦都不能彻底解决。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: We can keep using the refractor — but if we want a cleaner image, we need a telescope that collects light WITHOUT passing it through a big lens. A reflector.
level_25_after.text_zh: 我们可以继续用折射镜——但如果想要更干净的图像，就需要一台不让光穿过大透镜的望远镜。反射式望远镜。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: Check the Mission Board, then meet me at the Assembly Table. The Newtonian parts are already in the cabinet.
level_25_after.text_zh: 先看看任务板，然后到组装台找我。牛顿镜的零件已经放进零件柜了。

first_tube_subassembly.speaker: Maya
first_tube_subassembly.text_en: One more thing before you touch that tube: the Optical Tube Assembly is a COMPONENT WITH AN INTERIOR. Click it to open the tube blueprint and install the mirrors inside.
first_tube_subassembly.text_zh: 碰那个镜筒之前再说一件事：光学镜筒是一个"有内部结构的组件"。点击它就能打开镜筒蓝图，在里面安装镜片。

first_tube_subassembly.speaker: Maya
first_tube_subassembly.text_en: Save the tube when it's complete and you'll come right back to this bench, with the tube shown as installed. You can reopen it anytime to check your work.
first_tube_subassembly.text_zh: 装完之后保存镜筒，你会直接回到这个装配台，镜筒会显示为已安装。之后你随时可以再点开它检查。

first_collimation.speaker: Maya
first_collimation.text_en: Before a reflector can observe, its mirrors must agree on ONE optical axis. That's collimation: tilting the primary and secondary until light lands dead center.
first_collimation.text_zh: 反射镜观测之前，它的几面镜子必须对齐在同一条光轴上。这就是准直：微调主镜和副镜，直到光线正中靶心。

first_collimation.speaker: Maya
first_collimation.text_en: A perfectly built Newtonian with bad collimation gives worse images than a cheap refractor. Take your time in there.
first_collimation.text_zh: 一台装配完美但准直糟糕的牛顿镜，成像还不如便宜的折射镜。进去以后慢慢来。

level_27_after.speaker: Maya
level_27_after.text_en: Same star, same sky — but no colored fringe this time. Mirrors reflect every color along the same path.
level_27_after.text_zh: 同一颗星，同一片天空——但这次没有彩色边缘了。镜面把所有颜色的光沿同一条路径反射。

level_27_after.speaker: Maya
level_27_after.text_en: But notice what it cost you: you had to build a tube full of precision mirrors and then collimate them. A reflector is not better at everything — it trades lens color error for alignment work.
level_27_after.text_zh: 但也注意它的代价：你得装好一整筒精密镜片，还要给它们准直。反射镜不是所有方面都更好——它用准直工作换掉了透镜的色差。

level_27_after.speaker: Maya
level_27_after.text_en: Next, let's see what this mirror is REALLY good at: faint, deep-sky targets.
level_27_after.text_zh: 接下来把它转向深空。镜面没有彩边，大口径也更适合收那些微弱的光。

level_30_before.speaker: Maya
level_30_before.text_en: Now leave the Solar System. The Crab Nebula is wreckage from a star about 6,500 light-years away; the 150mm mirror gives your dark-adapted eye enough photons to find it.
level_30_before.text_zh: 现在离开太阳系。蟹状星云是约 6,500 光年外一颗恒星留下的残骸；150mm 主镜为暗适应后的眼睛收集到足够光子。

level_30_after.speaker: Maya
level_30_after.text_en: A planet is bright because it is nearby. A supernova remnant is meaningful because every faint filament crossed thousands of years to reach you.
level_30_after.text_zh: 行星明亮，是因为它们近；超新星遗迹的每一缕微光都穿越了数千年才到达你。

level_26_after.speaker: Maya
level_26_after.text_en: First light through mirrors - and the Moon never looked cleaner. Log it: this is what a collimated reflector gives you.
level_26_after.text_zh: 镜面的第一束光——月球从未这么干净过。记下来：这就是一台准直到位的反射镜给你的回报。

level_27_before.speaker: Maya
level_27_before.text_en: Back to Vega - the same star that betrayed the lens in L23. Look at its edge through mirrors this time.
level_27_before.text_zh: 回到织女星——就是在 L23 出卖了透镜的那颗星。这次透过镜面看它的边缘。

level_28_before.speaker: Maya
level_28_before.text_en: Saturn is our first useful focus test: its ring has a real edge. The Newtonian should make that edge sharp without painting it red or blue.
level_28_before.text_zh: 拿土星练调焦正合适。盯住光环边缘，调到干净利落，而且不该再有红蓝彩边。

level_28_after.speaker: Maya
level_28_after.text_en: You did not just make Saturn larger. You separated a real structure without adding false color.
level_28_after.text_zh: 你不只是放大了土星，而是在不增加虚假颜色的前提下分开了真实结构。

level_29_before.speaker: Maya
level_29_before.text_en: Albireo looks like one star to the eye. A collimated mirror turns it into a gold-and-blue pair, so alignment finally has a visible consequence.
level_29_before.text_zh: 辇道增七用肉眼看像一颗星。准直到位的镜面会把它分成金蓝双星，所以准直终于有了直接可见的结果。

level_29_after.speaker: Maya
level_29_after.text_en: That clean split is angular resolution, not decoration. A miscollimated telescope would smear the pair together.
level_29_after.text_zh: 这次清楚分离来自角分辨率。准直不良会把双星重新糊成一团。

level_31_before.speaker: Maya
level_31_before.text_en: The Sombrero Galaxy is almost 30 million light-years away. Do not zoom harder. Preserve brightness, adapt your eyes, and look beside the dust lane.
level_31_before.text_zh: 草帽星系距离近 3,000 万光年。不要一味放大；保留亮度、完成暗适应，并看向暗尘带旁边。

level_31_after.speaker: Maya
level_31_after.text_en: You held a nucleus and dust lane from another galaxy. That is the 150mm mirror doing work no small bright-target lesson could show.
level_31_after.text_zh: 你持续看见了另一个星系的亮核与暗尘带。这才是 150mm 主镜在明亮近邻目标上无法展示的能力。

level_32_before.speaker: Maya
level_32_before.text_en: Uranus is where clean color, precise focus, and manual drift correction meet. The victory is proving that the blue-green point has a disk.
level_32_before.text_zh: 天王星很小，也很容易漂走。先稳住再细调焦，直到蓝绿色光点露出圆面。

level_32_after.speaker: Maya
level_32_after.text_en: A difficult observation can be a tiny distinction. You separated a planet from the field stars by shape and color.
level_32_after.text_zh: 困难观测可能只是一点细微差别。你通过形状与颜色把行星从背景恒星中分辨出来了。

level_33_before.speaker: Maya
level_33_before.text_en: The Dumbbell is broad enough to survive poor seeing, but sky glow hides its shell. Tonight the filter matters more than magnification.
level_33_before.text_zh: 哑铃星云足够宽广，不会被差视宁度完全抹掉，但天空背景会藏住外壳。今晚滤镜比倍率更重要。

level_33_after.speaker: Maya
level_33_after.text_en: Different targets ask different questions. You solved contrast instead of trying to overpower the atmosphere.
level_33_after.text_zh: 这个目标缺的是对比度，不是倍率。先把背景压暗，别跟大气硬碰硬。

level_85_before.speaker: Maya
level_85_before.text_en: FAST final: show me a complete, defensible radio detection.
level_85_before.text_zh: FAST 最后一练。把干扰清干净，让周期、色散量和信噪比都对得上。

level_85_after.speaker: Maya
level_85_after.text_en: Visible, infrared, radio — you can now observe in three windows of the electromagnetic spectrum. One question remains: what happens when we point ALL of them at the same target?
level_85_after.text_zh: 可见光、红外、无线电，你都用过了。下一晚，让三台仪器一起看同一个目标。

level_84_before.speaker: Maya
level_84_before.text_en: Full radio session, solo: tune, localize, measure, record.
level_84_before.text_zh: 这次你独立值班：调谐、定位、测量，最后把结果记下来。

level_84_after.speaker: Maya
level_84_after.text_en: From eyepieces to data traces - and you read both fluently now.
level_84_after.text_zh: 你已经会看目镜里的细节，也会读屏幕上的脉冲了。

level_83_before.speaker: Maya
level_83_before.text_en: Interference is our light pollution: phones, satellites, engines. Learn the pulsar's voice among them.
level_83_before.text_zh: 手机、卫星、发动机都会挤进频谱。先把这些人造干扰挑出去，别误删那条重复的候选信号。

level_83_after.speaker: Maya
level_83_after.text_en: Nature repeats precisely; humans repeat messily. Now you can hear the difference.
level_83_after.text_zh: 脉冲星的节拍会稳定重复，人造干扰常常带着固定窄峰或杂乱突发。你已经会分了。

level_82_before.speaker: Maya
level_82_before.text_en: The feed cabin hangs from six cables above the dish. Position it finely against a turning sky.
level_82_before.text_zh: 用方向控制慢慢推馈源舱，接近目标就提前刹车。六根缆索吊着它，松手以后还会滑一段。

level_82_after.speaker: Maya
level_82_after.text_en: A 30-ton cabin, placed with millimeter care. Engineering is astronomy's other half.
level_82_after.text_zh: 三十吨的馈源舱终于稳住了。这么大的设备，也得一点点收进锁定环。

level_81_before.speaker: Maya
level_81_before.text_en: Let the trace accumulate. In radio astronomy, time literally adds up to certainty.
level_81_before.text_zh: 按住积分，先别松手。时间越长，随机噪声会慢慢退下去。

level_81_after.speaker: Maya
level_81_after.text_en: The longer you listened, the clearer the heartbeat. Patience is an instrument.
level_81_after.text_zh: 再多积一会儿。那道脉冲已经快从噪声里站出来了。

level_80_before.speaker: Maya
level_80_before.text_en: Tonight the pulse barely clears the noise floor. Finer tuning, slower reading.
level_80_before.text_zh: 今晚的脉冲只比噪声高一点。频窗再收准些，积分也要更久。

level_80_after.speaker: Maya
level_80_after.text_zh: 信号越弱，越不能靠猜。每一步读数都得对得上。

level_79_before.speaker: Maya
level_79_before.text_en: Final radio exercise: localize the source. A radio telescope 'points' by moving its feed cabin and reading signal strength. Find where the pulse is strongest — that's your pulsar's position.
level_79_before.text_zh: 最后练一次射电定位。移动馈源舱，盯着信号强度；峰值最高的位置，就是源的方向。

level_79_before.speaker: Maya
level_79_before.text_en: No stars to hop between this time. The signal meter is your finder scope.
level_79_before.text_zh: 这里没有星点可点。看信号强度表，它就是 FAST 的寻星镜。

level_79_after.speaker: Maya
level_79_after.text_en: You pointed a telescope with a strength meter instead of your eyes. Welcome to radio astronomy.
level_79_after.text_zh: 定位完成。你没看见那颗星，却靠信号强度把望远镜指向了它。

level_78_before.speaker: Maya
level_78_before.text_en: Pulsar B0329+54: a neutron star spinning at 1.4 revolutions per second. On your trace it appears as a repeating pulse. Tune the band, watch the peaks, measure the period.
level_78_before.text_zh: 目标是脉冲星 B0329+54，每秒大约转 1.4 圈。先调好频段，再从重复峰值里量出它的周期。

level_78_before.speaker: Maya
level_78_before.text_en: There is no image here. The DATA is the observation.
level_78_before.text_zh: FAST 不会给你拍一张照片。看频谱和脉冲，规律就藏在这些曲线里。

level_78_after.speaker: Maya
level_78_after.text_en: A rhythm from a city-sized star three thousand light-years away. When Jocelyn Bell first saw this pattern in 1967, her team jokingly labeled it LGM-1: 'Little Green Men'.
level_78_after.text_zh: 来自三千光年外一颗城市大小恒星的节拍。1967 年乔斯林·贝尔第一次看到这种信号时，团队开玩笑地把它标记为 LGM-1——"小绿人一号"。

level_77_before.speaker: Maya
level_77_before.text_en: Sweep the band slowly. Somewhere in the noise, a dead star is knocking.
level_77_before.text_zh: 慢慢扫频，别一下拉到底。噪声里那条稳定重复的峰，就是我们要找的。

level_77_after.speaker: Maya
level_77_after.text_en: There it is - the knock. 1.4 times per second, for millions of years.
level_77_after.text_zh: 找到了。大约每秒 1.4 次，和预期周期对上了。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: This is FAST — the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope in Guizhou, China. The largest single dish on Earth. And it has NO eyepiece. Nothing to look through at all.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: 这是 FAST——位于中国贵州的五百米口径球面射电望远镜，地球上最大的单口径天线。它没有目镜，完全没有可以"看"的地方。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: Radio waves from space are collected by the dish, focused onto the feed cabin hanging above it, and turned into electrical signals a processor can record.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: 来自太空的无线电波被反射面收集，聚焦到悬吊在上方的馈源舱，再转换成信号处理器可以记录的电信号。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: Set up the link: active dish, feed cabin, signal processor. Forget focusing — from now on you TUNE, you don't focus.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: 把链路搭起来：主动反射面、馈源舱、信号处理器。忘掉调焦吧——从现在起，你要做的是调谐，不是对焦。

level_76_after.speaker: Maya
level_76_after.text_en: The link is live. Somewhere out there, a dead star is sweeping a radio beam across the Earth like a lighthouse. Tomorrow, we catch it.
level_76_after.text_zh: 链路开通了。在遥远的某处，一颗死去的恒星正像灯塔一样，用无线电波束扫过地球。明天，我们去抓住它。

level_75_before.speaker: Maya
level_75_before.text_en: Last infrared night. After this, we listen to the sky instead of looking at it.
level_75_before.text_zh: 最后一个红外之夜。在这之后，我们不再"看"天空，而是"听"它。

level_75_after.speaker: Maya
level_75_after.text_en: Cold instruments, clean signal. You now understand light our eyes can't see. But there's radiation even 'colder' than infrared — radio waves. And for those, we have a giant.
level_75_after.text_zh: 你已经不只是在“看”了。红外这边，冷、热、尘埃，都会留下线索。接下来还有无线电，那要交给一台更大的家伙。

level_74_before.speaker: Maya
level_74_before.text_en: Run tonight's infrared session yourself: deploy, cool, point, observe. I am only watching.
level_74_before.text_zh: 今晚的红外观测全由你来：部署、降温、指向、观测。我只旁观。

level_74_after.speaker: Maya
level_74_after.text_en: Flawless. You operate a space telescope the way you once operated a 60mm refractor.
level_74_after.text_zh: 无可挑剔。你操作空间望远镜,就像当年操作 60mm 折射镜一样自然。

level_73_before.speaker: Maya
level_73_before.text_en: Betelgeuse is cool, red, and enormous - a natural infrared beacon. Measure the giant.
level_73_before.text_zh: 参宿四又冷又红又巨大——天生的红外灯塔。测量这颗巨星。

level_73_after.speaker: Maya
level_73_after.text_en: A star too cool to dazzle your eyes, blazing in the infrared. Temperature is a point of view.
level_73_after.text_zh: 一颗冷得晃不了你眼睛的恒星,在红外里却光芒万丈。温度是一种视角。

level_72_before.speaker: Maya
level_72_before.text_en: Pull out your Newtonian records of Orion. Compare them with tonight and name what the atmosphere stole.
level_72_before.text_zh: 翻出你牛顿镜的猎户座记录。和今晚对比,说出大气偷走了什么。

level_72_after.speaker: Maya
level_72_after.text_en: Now you know exactly what leaving the atmosphere buys. It is written in your own two records.
level_72_after.text_zh: 现在你确切知道离开大气层买到了什么。答案写在你自己的两份记录里。

level_71_before.speaker: Maya
level_71_before.text_en: Map Andromeda's warm dust lanes tonight - structure no ground telescope of ours can touch.
level_71_before.text_zh: 今晚描绘仙女座温暖的尘埃带——我们任何地面望远镜都碰不到的结构。

level_71_after.speaker: Maya
level_71_after.text_en: A galaxy's skeleton, drawn in heat. Add it to the three portraits you are collecting.
level_71_after.text_zh: 用热画出的星系骨架。把它加进你正在收集的肖像里。

level_70_before.speaker: Maya
level_70_before.text_en: Today's lesson is the sunshield itself. Point the model so the shield blocks the Sun, Earth and Moon all at once. If the instruments warm up even slightly, their own heat drowns the signal.
level_70_before.text_zh: 今天先不急着拍图。先把遮阳板摆对，不然仪器自己发热就会把信号盖掉。

level_70_after.speaker: Maya
level_70_after.text_en: Pointing AND shading at once - now you think like a spacecraft operator.
level_70_after.text_zh: 指向和遮挡同时成立——你已经开始像航天器操作员一样思考了。

level_69_before.speaker: Maya
level_69_before.text_en: An infrared telescope that isn't cold is just an expensive heater looking at itself.
level_69_before.text_zh: 一台不够冷的红外望远镜，只是一台看着自己发呆的昂贵加热器。

level_69_after.speaker: Maya
level_69_after.text_en: Cold instruments, clean signal. Heat management IS observation in the infrared.
level_69_after.text_zh: 温度稳住了，背景也安静了。做红外观测，先把仪器照顾冷，后面才有干净图像。

level_68_before.speaker: Maya
level_68_before.text_en: The Orion Nebula again — but in infrared this time. Visible light shows you the glowing gas. Infrared passes THROUGH the dust and shows you the newborn stars hiding inside.
level_68_before.text_zh: 又是猎户座大星云——但这次用红外线看。可见光给你看发光的气体，红外线则能穿透尘埃，让你看到藏在里面的新生恒星。

level_68_after.speaker: Maya
level_68_after.text_en: Stars that no eyepiece on Earth could ever show you — because their light never reaches the ground as visible light at all.
level_68_after.text_zh: 这些恒星是地球上任何目镜都永远看不到的——因为它们的光根本不会以可见光的形式到达地面。

level_67_before.speaker: Maya
level_67_before.text_en: You're not magnifying harder. You're asking a different question: not 'what shines?' but 'what is warm?'
level_67_before.text_zh: 这次别只看哪里亮。红外更擅长找温暖的尘埃，以及藏在尘埃里的恒星。

level_67_after.speaker: Maya
level_67_after.text_en: You asked 'what is warm' and the sky answered differently. Keep both answers.
level_67_after.text_zh: 你问了"什么是温热的"，天空给出了不同的回答。两个答案都留着。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: Meet a segmented space telescope, like the James Webb. Its primary mirror is not one disc but many hexagonal segments folded for launch.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 先看分段式空间望远镜，詹姆斯·韦伯就是这种设计。主镜不是一整块，而是能折叠发射的六边形镜片。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: It does not form an eyepiece image of visible light. It reads INFRARED - the heat of dust-shrouded nurseries and the coldest, most distant galaxies.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 它不形成可见光的目镜图像，而是读取红外——尘埃笼罩的恒星摇篮、以及最冷最遥远星系的热辐射。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: Assemble the hexagonal segments, the deployable secondary, the five-layer sunshield and the infrared instrument bay, then align and deploy them.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 组装六边形分段主镜、可展开副镜、五层遮阳罩和红外仪器舱，再完成对准与展开。

level_66_after.speaker: Maya
level_66_after.text_en: Segments aligned, sunshield deployed. In space this alignment took engineers three months. You get the idea in one evening — not bad.
level_66_after.text_zh: 镜片对齐，遮阳板展开。在太空中，工程师花了三个月做这次对齐。你一个晚上就理解了它的原理——不错。

level_65_before.speaker: Maya
level_65_before.text_en: Last night with the mirror family: Mars, with the Gregorian. Newtonian, Cassegrain, Gregorian — each fold has a reason. Tonight, prove you can drive any of them.
level_65_before.text_zh: 镜面家族的最后一晚：用格里高利式看火星。牛顿式、卡塞格林式、格里高利式——每一种折叠都有它的理由。今晚，证明你能驾驭它们中的任何一台。

level_65_after.speaker: Maya
level_65_after.text_en: You've mastered every ground-based mirror we own. But everything we did tonight fought the same enemy: the atmosphere itself. Turbulence, clouds, glow.
level_65_after.text_zh: 我们拥有的每一台地面反射镜你都掌握了。但今晚我们做的一切都在对抗同一个敌人：大气本身。湍流、云层、天光。

level_65_after.speaker: Maya
level_65_after.text_en: What if the telescope simply... left the atmosphere behind? Come back tomorrow. I have something special to show you.
level_65_after.text_zh: 如果望远镜干脆……离开大气层呢？明天再来。我有特别的东西给你看。

level_64_before.speaker: Maya
level_64_before.text_en: Golden Arcturus, and a review: Newtonian, Cassegrain, Gregorian. Tell me why each fold exists.
level_64_before.text_zh: 金色的大角星，加一场复习：牛顿、卡塞格林、格里高利。告诉我每种折叠为什么存在。

level_64_after.speaker: Maya
level_64_after.text_en: Three folds, three reasons, one observer who understands all of them.
level_64_after.text_zh: 三种折叠、三个理由、一个全都理解的观测者。

level_63_before.speaker: Maya
level_63_before.text_en: Poor seeing on the strictest instrument we own. Learn which errors are yours and which belong to the sky.
level_63_before.text_zh: 最严苛的仪器遇上糟糕的视宁度。分清哪些误差是你的，哪些属于天空。

level_63_after.speaker: Maya
level_63_after.text_en: Tonight you separated instrument error from atmosphere. Few observers ever learn the difference.
level_63_after.text_zh: 今晚你分清了仪器误差和大气误差。很多观测者一辈子都没学会。

level_62_before.speaker: Maya
level_62_before.text_en: Drift correction through a folded path now. Keep Sirius centered.
level_62_before.text_zh: 现在在折叠光路里做漂移修正。让天狼星保持居中。

level_62_after.speaker: Maya
level_62_after.text_en: Steady through the fold. Your corrections are getting invisible - that is the goal.
level_62_after.text_zh: 折叠光路中依然稳定。你的修正正在变得不可察觉——这正是目标。

level_61_before.speaker: Maya
level_61_before.text_en: Can a strict two-mirror fold handle a faint nebula? Tonight we find out.
level_61_before.text_zh: 严苛的双镜折叠能应付暗弱星云吗？今晚见分晓。

level_61_after.speaker: Maya
level_61_after.text_en: It held. Precision and light-gathering are not enemies - just an expensive friendship.
level_61_after.text_zh: 它扛住了。精密和集光并不敌对——只是这份友谊比较昂贵。

level_60_before.speaker: Maya
level_60_before.text_en: Study Jupiter's cloud bands tonight. Contrast - not size - is what this design defends.
level_60_before.text_zh: 今晚研究木星云带。这个设计守护的不是大小，是对比度。

level_60_after.speaker: Maya
level_60_after.text_en: The bands separated cleanly. Contrast is a quality you feel before you can measure it.
level_60_after.text_zh: 云带分得干干净净。对比度是一种先感觉到、后测量到的品质。

level_59_before.speaker: Maya
level_59_before.text_en: Mars tolerates no sloppiness through this instrument. Check your alignment before you blame the sky.
level_59_before.text_zh: 这台仪器上,火星不容忍任何马虎。怪天空之前先检查你的对准。

level_59_after.speaker: Maya
level_59_after.text_en: Strict optics teach honest observers. You are becoming one.
level_59_after.text_zh: 严苛的光学教出诚实的观测者。你正在成为其中之一。

level_58_before.speaker: Maya
level_58_before.text_en: Vega one more time. Upright, high-contrast, fringe-free - the Gregorian's quiet signature.
level_58_before.text_zh: 再看一次织女星。正立、高对比、无彩边——这是格里高利镜低调的签名。

level_58_after.speaker: Maya
level_58_after.text_en: Three telescopes have now shown you the same star three ways. Keep all three records.
level_58_after.text_zh: 三台望远镜已经用三种方式给你看了同一颗星。三份记录都留好。

level_57_before.speaker: Maya
level_57_before.text_en: Sirius again — you observed it with the refractor long ago. Same star, different physics. Pay attention to where the focus 'snaps in' compared to what you remember.
level_57_before.text_zh: 又是天狼星——很久以前你用折射镜看过它。同一颗星，不同的物理。注意它"咔哒"合焦的位置和你记忆中的差别。

level_57_after.speaker: Maya
level_57_after.text_en: A tighter, cleaner point than the refractor ever gave you — and no purple halo. Focus position is a property of the OPTICS, not just of your fingers.
level_57_after.text_zh: 比折射镜给过你的更紧致、更干净的星点——而且没有紫色光晕。合焦位置是光学系统的属性，不只是你手指的功劳。

level_56_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_56_before_assembly.text_en: The Gregorian uses a CONCAVE secondary mirror placed BEYOND the primary's focus. The light comes to a focus, spreads out again, and only then hits the secondary.
level_56_before_assembly.text_zh: 格里高利式使用一面凹面副镜，放在主镜焦点的更远处。光先聚成一个焦点，再散开，然后才碰到副镜。

level_56_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_56_before_assembly.text_en: That extra focus point makes the image upright — sailors loved it centuries ago — but it demands stricter alignment: two curved mirrors AND a mid-air focal point must all agree.
level_56_before_assembly.text_zh: 多出来的这个焦点让成像是正立的——几百年前的航海家很喜欢这一点——但它对光轴要求更严格：两面曲面镜和一个悬在半空的焦点必须完全一致。

level_56_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_56_before_assembly.text_en: This is not 'a fancier telescope'. It's a different geometry with its own price. Assemble it and feel the difference.
level_56_before_assembly.text_zh: 格里高利式的光路和前几台不一样，也有自己的代价。先把它装好，再从画面里体会差别。

level_56_after.speaker: Maya
level_56_after.text_en: Two curved mirrors, one mid-air focus, zero fringe. Feel how much stricter the alignment wanted to be.
level_56_after.text_zh: 两面曲面镜、一个悬空焦点、零彩边。感受一下它的对准要求严格了多少。

level_55_before.speaker: Maya
level_55_before.text_en: Cassegrain final: folded optics under real conditions. Everything counts tonight.
level_55_before.text_zh: 卡塞格林结业考：真实条件下的折叠光学。今晚每一项都算分。

level_55_after.speaker: Maya
level_55_after.text_en: You've now folded visible light with mirrors two ways: straight through with a Newtonian, and doubled back with the Cassegrain.
level_55_after.text_zh: 你已经用镜面折叠可见光两种方式：牛顿镜直穿、卡塞格林镜折返。

level_55_after.speaker: Maya
level_55_after.text_en: But the universe does not shine only in visible light. Some objects are hidden behind dust; some star-forming regions are almost dark to our eyes.
level_55_after.text_zh: 但宇宙并不只用可见光发光。有些天体被尘埃遮挡，有些恒星形成区在可见光下几乎是暗的。

level_55_after.speaker: Maya
level_55_after.text_en: Infrared - heat radiation - passes through some of that dust and reveals the warmth beneath. For that, we leave the ground and go to space.
level_55_after.text_zh: 红外线——热辐射——能穿过部分尘埃，显示其下的温度。为此，我们要离开地面，走向太空。

level_54_before.speaker: Maya
level_54_before.text_en: Clouds cross a narrow field fast and completely. Time your observation between them.
level_54_before.text_zh: 云穿过窄视场又快又彻底。在云缝之间安排观测。

level_54_after.speaker: Maya
level_54_after.text_en: Narrow field, narrow windows. You used both well.
level_54_after.text_zh: 窄视场,窄窗口。你两个都用好了。

level_53_before.speaker: Maya
level_53_before.text_en: Same Jupiter, two mirrors. Compare your Newtonian log with tonight - honestly.
level_53_before.text_zh: 同一颗木星，两种镜子。把牛顿镜的记录和今晚的对比——要诚实。

level_53_after.speaker: Maya
level_53_after.text_en: Wide and bright versus large and detailed. Neither wins everywhere - instruments are choices, not upgrades.
level_53_after.text_zh: 宽而亮对阵大而细。没有全场获胜者——仪器是选择，不是升级。

level_52_before.speaker: Maya
level_52_before.text_en: Turn all that focal length on the Moon. Single craters will fill your eyepiece.
level_52_before.text_zh: 把这一整段焦距对准月球。单个环形山就能填满你的目镜。

level_52_after.speaker: Maya
level_52_after.text_en: You walked the rim of a single crater tonight. That is what folded focal length buys.
level_52_after.text_zh: 今晚你沿着一座环形山的边缘走了一圈。这就是折叠焦距买来的东西。

level_51_before.speaker: Maya
level_51_before.text_en: At this magnification the sky RACES across the field. Keep Mars centered - corrections small and quick.
level_51_before.text_zh: 在这个倍率下，天空在视场里飞奔。让火星保持居中——修正要小要快。

level_51_after.speaker: Maya
level_51_after.text_en: Drift scales with power. You just proved it with your own hands.
level_51_after.text_zh: 漂移随倍率放大。你刚用自己的手证明了这一点。

level_50_before.speaker: Maya
level_50_before.text_en: High power is a deal with the atmosphere. Tonight the air is against you - negotiate.
level_50_before.text_zh: 高倍率是和大气做的交易。今晚大气不配合——去谈判吧。

level_50_after.speaker: Maya
level_50_after.text_en: You waited for the still moments and they came. High power rewards patience, not force.
level_50_after.text_zh: 你等到了平静的瞬间。高倍率回报的是耐心，不是蛮力。

level_49_before.speaker: Maya
level_49_before.text_en: Mars is small and low tonight — the harshest test for a folded telescope. Use everything you know: careful finding, patient focus, waiting out the turbulence.
level_49_before.text_zh: 今晚的火星又小又低——这是对折叠望远镜最苛刻的考验。用上你会的一切：仔细寻星、耐心调焦、等待大气平静。

level_49_after.speaker: Maya
level_49_after.text_en: Small disk, long focus, honest result. Log what the air allowed.
level_49_after.text_zh: 小圆面、长焦距、诚实的结果。把大气允许你看到的记下来。

level_48_before.speaker: Maya
level_48_before.text_en: A narrow field punishes sloppy aiming. Tonight the finder scope earns its keep again.
level_48_before.text_zh: 窄视场惩罚粗糙的瞄准。今晚寻星镜又要立功了。

level_48_after.speaker: Maya
level_48_after.text_en: Found it clean. Old skills never expire - they just meet harder telescopes.
level_48_after.text_zh: 干净利落地找到了。老本事不会过期——它们只是遇到了更难的望远镜。

level_47_before.speaker: Maya
level_47_before.text_en: Jupiter under long focal length: the disk will look bigger than you've ever seen it. But the narrow field means careful finding, and the seeing will shimmer at high power.
level_47_before.text_zh: 长焦距下的木星：圆面会比你以往见过的都大。但窄视场意味着寻星要更仔细，而且高倍率下大气视宁度会让它微微晃动。

level_47_before.speaker: Maya
level_47_before.text_en: If the image boils, don't fight it — wait for the still moments.
level_47_before.text_zh: 如果图像在"沸腾"，别硬扛——等那些短暂的稳定瞬间。

level_47_after.speaker: Maya
level_47_after.text_en: Cloud bands at high power — worth every bit of careful aiming. High magnification is a deal with the atmosphere: it shows more only when the air allows.
level_47_after.text_zh: 高倍率下的云带——所有仔细的瞄准都值了。高倍率是和大气做的交易：只有空气允许时，它才让你看到更多。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: A Cassegrain hides a long telescope inside a short tube. The primary mirror sends light to a convex secondary, which bounces it BACK through a hole in the primary.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 卡塞格林把一台长望远镜藏进短镜筒里。主镜把光送到一面凸面副镜上，副镜再把光反射回来，穿过主镜中央的开孔。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: Folding the path doubles up the focal length in a compact body. Long focal length means high magnification with the same eyepieces.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 折叠光路让长焦距装进紧凑的机身。长焦距意味着同样的目镜能得到更高的倍率。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: The catch: a narrow field of view, and high power magnifies every wobble and every ripple of the atmosphere. Build it, then aim carefully.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 代价是：视场很窄，而且高倍率会放大每一次晃动和大气的每一丝抖动。先装好它，然后瞄准时要格外仔细。

level_46_after.speaker: Maya
level_46_after.text_en: Compact outside, long inside. Now let us see what a folded light path does to a planet.
level_46_after.text_zh: 外面紧凑，里面很长。现在看看折叠光路对行星能做什么。

level_45_before.speaker: Maya
level_45_before.text_en: Return to the Dumbbell for the final comparison. The 150mm showed the bright hourglass; the 200mm should add the faint outer shell while you track manually.
level_45_before.text_zh: 结业时重访哑铃星云。150mm 显出了明亮沙漏；200mm 应在手动追踪中补出暗弱外壳。

level_45_after.speaker: Maya
level_45_after.text_en: The Dobsonian did not repeat the Newtonian. It reached fainter planets, resolved a globular cluster, framed wider fields, and held galaxies tens of millions of light-years away.
level_45_after.text_zh: 多布森没有重复牛顿镜。它触及更暗的行星、分解球状星团、容纳更宽视场，并稳住数千万光年外的星系。

level_44_before.speaker: Maya
level_44_before.text_en: M51 is about 23 million light-years away. Its companion is not a second target; gravity has made both galaxies one interacting system.
level_44_before.text_zh: M51 距离约 2,300 万光年。伴星系不是第二个无关目标；引力让两个星系成为相互作用的系统。

level_44_after.speaker: Maya
level_44_after.text_en: You held both cores and a hint of connection by hand. This is exactly the kind of faint structure the 200mm mirror was built for.
level_44_after.text_zh: 你用双手保住了两个亮核与一丝连接结构。这正是 200mm 主镜存在的意义。

level_43_before.speaker: Maya
level_43_before.text_en: Neptune is dimmer than any naked-eye planet. Finder star-hopping gets you there; the 200mm mirror and patient focus prove which blue point is the planet.
level_43_before.text_zh: 海王星比任何肉眼行星都暗。寻星镜跳星把你带到附近；200mm 主镜和耐心调焦证明哪个蓝点才是行星。

level_43_after.speaker: Maya
level_43_after.text_en: You reached the Solar System frontier without a computerized mount. Aperture and navigation worked together.
level_43_after.text_zh: 你在没有电脑支架的情况下抵达了太阳系边疆。口径与导航协同完成了任务。

level_42_before.speaker: Maya
level_42_before.text_en: NGC 4565 is about 40 million light-years away and nearly edge-on. The challenge is holding its long silver disk and dark lane while low-altitude air keeps softening them.
level_42_before.text_zh: NGC 4565 距离约 4,000 万光年，几乎完全侧向。挑战是在低空气流不断软化图像时，仍保住细长银色星系盘与暗尘带。

level_42_after.speaker: Maya
level_42_after.text_en: That thin disk is farther than any target in the Newtonian chapter. The 200mm upgrade revealed structure instead of merely enlarging a blur.
level_42_after.text_zh: 那片细长星系盘比牛顿镜章节的任何目标都更遥远。200mm 升级显出了结构，而不是只把模糊放大。

level_41_before.speaker: Maya
level_41_before.text_en: The Ring Nebula returns for a fair comparison, but cloud gaps are short. Prepare before the sky opens.
level_41_before.text_zh: 环状星云回来做一次公平对比，但云缝很短。要在天空打开之前准备完毕。

level_41_after.speaker: Maya
level_41_after.text_en: The 200mm mirror recovered the ring faster through each gap. More light can buy observing time, not just detail.
level_41_after.text_zh: 200mm 主镜在每次云缝中都更快找回星云环。更多光线不仅购买细节，也购买有效观测时间。

level_40_before.speaker: Maya
level_40_before.text_en: The Lagoon is broad and faint. Use the 30mm eyepiece and filter; the goal is to keep its dark lane inside the whole luminous cloud.
level_40_before.text_zh: 礁湖星云又宽又淡。用 30mm 目镜和滤镜，把暗带和周围发光云气一起留在视野里。

level_40_after.speaker: Maya
level_40_after.text_en: A large telescope does not always mean high power. Tonight aperture bought brightness and the eyepiece protected the field.
level_40_after.text_zh: 大望远镜并不总意味着高倍率。今晚口径换来亮度，而目镜保护了视场。

level_39_before.speaker: Maya
level_39_before.text_en: M13 contains hundreds of thousands of stars about 22,200 light-years away. The larger mirror should begin to break its fuzzy edge into grains.
level_39_before.text_zh: M13 在约 22,200 光年外包含数十万颗恒星。更大主镜应开始把模糊外缘分解成颗粒。

level_39_after.speaker: Maya
level_39_after.text_en: That resolved halo is the cleanest proof of aperture so far: 200mm revealed stars where 150mm mostly showed glow.
level_39_after.text_zh: 注意星团外缘。150mm 时那里多半只是一片微光，换到 200mm 后，边缘会开始分出一颗颗星。

level_38_before.speaker: Maya
level_38_before.text_en: The Double Cluster is 7,500 light-years away and wider than a planet. Hold both star cities together instead of chasing one bright member.
level_38_before.text_zh: 英仙座双星团距离约 7,500 光年，而且比行星宽广得多。让两座星城共同留在视野，不要追逐单颗亮星。

level_38_after.speaker: Maya
level_38_after.text_en: Wide-field manual tracking is its own skill. You preserved a composition, not just a center point.
level_38_after.text_zh: 宽视场手动追踪是一种独立技巧。你保住的是整体构图，而不只是中心点。

level_37_before.speaker: Maya
level_37_before.text_en: Revisit Saturn for one deliberate comparison. The 200mm view is brighter, but now your hands must replace the motor.
level_37_before.text_zh: 有意重访一次土星作对比。200mm 视野更亮，但现在你的双手必须代替马达。

level_37_after.speaker: Maya
level_37_after.text_en: The ring stayed detailed because you learned the Dobsonian rhythm: nudge, release, observe.
level_37_after.text_zh: 光环保持清晰，是因为你掌握了多布森节奏：轻推、松手、观察。

level_36_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_36_before_assembly.text_en: A Dobsonian keeps the Newtonian light path but spends its budget on a 200mm mirror and a simple rocker box. First frame the Pleiades: more light is useful only if you keep enough sky around it.
level_36_before_assembly.text_zh: 多布森保留牛顿式光路，把预算更多留给 200mm 主镜和简单摇箱。先用宽视场框住昴星团，别让大口径只换来一小块天空。

level_36_after.speaker: Maya
level_36_after.text_en: Both clusters and their outskirts fit. The Dobsonian lesson begins with aperture plus field, not a bigger copy of the Moon.
level_36_after.text_zh: 星团核心与外围都留在了视场里。多布森第一课是口径与视场，而不是一幅更大的月球复制品。

level_35_before.speaker: Maya
level_35_before.text_en: For graduation, find the Ring Nebula: much smaller and fainter than Orion. Collimation, filter, dark adaptation, and averted vision all have to agree.
level_35_before.text_zh: 结业目标是环状星云：它比猎户座星云小得多、暗得多。准直、滤镜、暗适应和侧视法必须同时到位。

level_35_after.speaker: Maya
level_35_after.text_en: The Newtonian chapter now spans the Moon, planets, double stars, stellar wreckage, nebulae, and another galaxy. That is a real optical upgrade.
level_35_after.text_zh: 牛顿镜这一路看过月球、行星、双星、恒星遗迹、星云和河外星系。大口径带来的变化，你已经亲眼看过了。

level_34_before.speaker: Maya
level_34_before.text_en: Tonight, Betelgeuse - a red supergiant. Through the old refractor its edge would bleed blue and red. Look at what your mirror shows instead.
level_34_before.text_zh: 今晚看参宿四——一颗红超巨星。透过旧折射镜，它的边缘会渗出红蓝杂色。看看你的镜面给出的是什么。

level_34_before.speaker: Maya
level_34_before.text_en: That deep orange is the star's OWN color: a surface cooler than our Sun. No lens is lying to you anymore.
level_34_before.text_zh: 那种深橙色是恒星自己的颜色：一个比太阳更冷的表面。再没有透镜对你说谎了。

level_34_after.speaker: Maya
level_34_after.text_en: You just read a star's temperature with your eyes - possible only because the mirror adds no false color. Tomorrow: your Newtonian final.
level_34_after.text_zh: 你刚用眼睛读出了一颗恒星的温度——这只有在镜面不添加虚假颜色时才可能。明天：牛顿镜结业考。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: Hold on - before you blame the telescope, look at the mission panel. Tonight's target is below the horizon.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 等一下——先别怪望远镜。看任务面板：今晚的目标此刻在地平线以下。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: Nothing is broken. The Earth is turning, and from our latitude this target simply hasn't risen right now.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 什么都没坏。地球在自转，从我们所在的纬度看，这个目标此刻根本还没升起来。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: Which stars are up depends on WHERE you stand on Earth and WHEN. Your latitude sets how high a target can ever climb.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 天上有哪些星，取决于你站在地球的哪个位置、什么时刻。你的纬度决定了目标最高能升到多高。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: So we do what real astronomers do: travel. Let's open the world map and find a site where it has already risen.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 那就换个观测地点。打开世界地图，找一座目标已经升起的观测站。
